name: Menno City Park Campground
note: City of Menno camper pads at the north end of the City Park on S Park St, with the park restroom just north of them; the city dump station is at the football field at the south end of Park St. No season is published (the city shut the site water off for winter on 2026-11-12); pay at the Finance Office, its drop box or online through paygov.us. --Claude
inclusion_evidence: City of Menno 'Camping Facilities' page (mennosd.org, read 2026-11-22; current, carries a '11/12/26' water-shutoff notice): 'There are six camp pads available at the north end of the City Park, on the west side of Menno. All have electrical hook-ups (50, 30 and 20 Amp). All 6 have water hook-ups, and a sewer dump. There is also a bath house facility that was completed in 2015. There are no reservations, sites are first come first serve at all times. There is a $25 per night fee for camping' (rate raised 2025-06-03 for the added water and sewer); the city's Parks page: 'Restroom facilities are located at the north end of the park, just past the camper pads'; the city map PDF (Menno_Map.pdf, 2016) labels 'CITY PARK & CAMPING' on S Park St -> a city campground on the town's own current page (public ladder step 1; local: no price gate or presence rule). Located on Esri imagery (2024-09-13 WV02, rendered): a ~30 x 33 m gravel lot on the SE side of S Park St with a small building at its north corner and a sand volleyball court beyond, matching 'restroom ... just past the camper pads'; Campendium's and The Dyrt's points (43.239724,-97.579478) fall on the same lot -> drive-in pads off a paved town street, room for a 23-ft rig. Not in the DB: the only entry within 10 km is 13556 Menno Lake Recreation Area, 3.5 km NW, which the same city page describes separately as association-run ('Menno Lake Camping - not affiliated with the City of Menno'). No 4WD, road, horse or long-stay wording anywhere.
waterfront_evidence: 2026-11-22: Esri World Imagery at 43.2385,-97.5800 (1.4 km frame), 43.2392,-97.5803 (220 m) and 43.23985,-97.5793 (z19 stitched), plus Esri Wayback 2024-09-13, 2021-10-15 and 2019-06-07 z19 at 43.2394,-97.5800; all rendered. The pads are a gravel lot in town between S Park St and a lumber/grain yard, among houses and town buildings; no water in the 220 m frame. The nearest water is a small creek channel in a tree band west of town, roughly 0.2-0.3 km west of the lot behind houses and yards and not visible from it -> not waterfront. (The Dyrt's generated blurb and one 2021 review say 'next to lake'; that describes Menno Lake, 3.5 km NW, entry 13556.)

fees.note: Pay at the Finance Office (236 S 5th St), its door drop box or the city hall drop box, or online at paygov.us (3% card fee).

fees_source: https://www.mennosd.org/index.asp?SEC=CBA0C25C-56B2-4EA4-971D-D75E823CE46B&DE=A54F0D14-6FB4-4CD7-BCA7-700FD3D502DB ('There is a $25 per night fee for camping.'; 'Increased rate went into effect on June 3, 2025, because of the addition of water and sewer at the camp spots.'), read 2026-11-22. The city's older Lodging/Camping page ($10) and Campendium/The Dyrt ($10) predate the 2025 increase.

curation_note: SD lead 19 (found p3-578 at 13556 Menno Lake; vetted 2026-11-22): the in-town city campground on the same City of Menno page, 3.5 km SE of 13556, whose 50 A / water / bath-house data had been mixed into 13556 until p3-578. Pin is my imagery read of the gravel lot (matches Campendium/The Dyrt), not a published site map. --Claude
flags: Pin: no published site map. The gravel lot on the SE side of S Park St (pin) fits the city's 'restroom ... just past the camper pads' (small building at its north corner) and Campendium/The Dyrt's point to 2 m. A second candidate was considered and rejected: a grassy lot ~110 m west across S Park St with 3-4 travel trailers parked in the 2021 and 2024 captures sits among house yards and a salvage-type lot and looks private. Google's 'Menno City Park' point (43.2381169,-97.5812665, 5.0 from 1 review, no phone) is the playground ~200 m SW at the park's south part. The reviewer may want a glance.

Imagery predates the 2025 water/sewer work (latest capture 2024-09-13), so the six pads are not individually visible; the lot is ~30 m deep, so a 23-ft rig fits, but pad lengths are unpublished. The Dyrt's '50 feet' and Campendium's 'Big rigs' are user/generated data, not used.

Season unpublished: season group omitted. Water at the pads was turned off 2026-11-12 'in preparation for winter'; the city says nothing about camping or electric over winter (unlike its Menno Lake notice).
Name: the city calls it camping/camper pads in the City Park; 'Menno City Park Campground' is my label (Campendium and The Dyrt list it as 'Menno City Park').
Phone is the City Finance Office line, which the city page lists for the whole site; no private individual's number used.
